column1: # Urdu numbers as IPA, which is the one thing a lexicon cannot hold: there
# are infinitely many numbers and this is the hundred words they are all
# built out of.
# 0 to 99 because Urdu's are irregular all the way up -- every one of them
# has its own name, unlike English, where twenty-one is two words. Then the
# five scale words, which are the Indian ones and not the Western: a hundred,
# a thousand, a lakh which is a hundred thousand, a crore which is a hundred
# lakh, and an arab which is a hundred crore. tools/urdu/numbers.py puts them
# together.
# Written by hand out of espeak's answers, once, because espeak reads a
# number written in ASCII digits and returns nothing at all for one written
# in Urdu's own numerals -- ۱۲۳ goes in and silence comes out. کروڑ is the
# one entry corrected: espeak wrote its retroflex as a full stop after the r,
# which is espeak's notation and not IPA.
سو
ہزار
